name: chessboard.jpg
title: File:Empty wooden chessboard.jpg
usage: The ask-before-you-tell slide for square numbers - eight squares along each side, so 8 x 8 = 64 squares on the board. Chosen because the object is already familiar, the grid is countable from the back of the room, and the white background sits cleanly on a light or dark slide. Cropped in from the original margins to fill a landscape split panel.

name: sugarcubes.jpg
title: File:Wurfelzucker -- 2018 -- 3564.jpg
usage: The ask-before-you-tell slide for cube numbers - a box packed 4 along each edge holds 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 cubes. Real cubes photographed next to the drawn cube stacks in CUBE_STACKS, so the class sees the object and the diagram of it side by side. High contrast on black, which projects well.

name: cubemelon.jpg
title: File:Square watermelon.jpg
usage: The deadpan word problem - Mr Bowen's cube watermelons, packed 3 along each edge of a crate, so 3 cubed = 27 melons. These are real: Japanese growers box the fruit as it grows. Read the slide completely straight. Cropped from the shop shelf to the melon itself so it fills a split panel.
